text:
alyssa: heads up — we saw another exporter index spike this morning, correlated with an increase in unique span attributes. looks like prompt_hash + full request_id + raw user identifiers are flowing into traces and the index cardinality exploded :grimacing:

kevin: ugh. which attributes exactly? prompt content, or the prompt_hash attr we added last quarter?

alyssa: both. some services still emit `prompt_text` in span.attrs for debug, and others emit `prompt_hash` without salting. request_id is full-uuid everywhere, and some mobile clients include `user_id` as a string.

maria: quick notes from product/compliance — we need enough fidelity to debug and link related spans (trace_id/request_id), but we can't keep raw PII or arbitrarily-unique keys in long-term datastore.

sam: thinking out loud: we can transform at the collector/exporter stage. options: hash(prompt_text) -> stable salt+truncate; replace request_id with bucketed id (e.g., prefix64 or hop-level id) so it still links within a request hop but doesn't create global cardinality; mark user_id as `hashed_user_id` and drop raw.

kevin: agree. implementation details matter: hashing prompt_text without salt allows cross-tenant correlation (bad). use per-tenant salt + key rotation. also need deterministic truncation length so we don't create many buckets accidentally.

alyssa: draft scrub config I've been prototyping for the otel-collector pipeline (staging):
```yaml
processors:
  attribute_scrubber/ruled:
    rules:
      - action: hash
        keys: ["prompt_text"]
        hash: hmac_sha256
        salt_key: tenant_id
        truncate: 16  # keep first 16 hex chars
      - action: bucketize
        keys: ["request_id"]
        method: prefix
        prefix_len: 8
      - action: redact_regex
        keys: ["user_email"]
        pattern: ".+@(.+)"
      - action: move
        keys: ["user_id"]
        target: "hashed_user_id"
        transform: hmac_sha256_trunc_12
      - action: drop_if_high_cardinality
        keys: ["prompt_trace_token"]
        threshold: 10000
exporters:
  logging/filtered:
    retention_days: 30
    index_tier: warm
```

kevin: looks reasonable. small comments: 1) `salt_key: tenant_id` is fine for hosted, but for private deployments we need opt-in or customer-managed salt (KMS). 2) `drop_if_high_cardinality` should emit a telemetry metric so we can audit how often we drop things.

maria: legal asks that we provide a way for customers to opt-out of any prompt hashing that might be needed for debugging (i.e., they can choose to keep original for a short TTL). add feature flag per-customer.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline: scrub-config v0.3 pushed to staging collector-cluster-7 by infra-ci at 2024-06-29T10:12:03Z

sam: followups on storage/retention: for high-cardinality attributes we should reduce retention to 7 days by default and allow per-tenant overrides. also prefer warm-tier with TTL-based compaction.

kevin: another thing — our dashboards (console/span search) rely on some attributes for filtering. we need a migration plan: either keep a small set of allowed filterable attributes (whitelist) or support search over hashed keys (with user-facing UX that explains hashed values). we should avoid sprinkling raw attributes into the index.

alyssa: proposal for rollout:
- stage 1: strict scrub in staging, test trace linking for a set of requests (compare pre/post).
- stage 2: canary in prod for low-traffic tenants with feature-flag off by default for enterprise/private.
- stage 3: enable for hosted tenants, run 7-day retention for scrubbed attrs, emit `telemetry.scrubber.drops` metric + per-tenant drop counts.
- stage 4: add UI in console to show which attributes are scrubbed and provide customer opt-out/short-ttl restore.

maria: +1. ensure we surface in contracts and data-processing agreements. also update SOC docs.

dataplane-bot: alert: exporter-idx-size increased 12% in cluster us-west2 at 2024-06-29T10:15:40Z; memory pressure rising

kevin: @alyssa can you add unit tests for salt rotation and a compatibility test that ensures truncated hashes don't collide often? we should simulate worst-case prompts (random vs similar).

alyssa: yes. I'll add tests and a small load-harness to simulate cardinality growth. also will add an audit log entry every time `drop_if_high_cardinality` triggers so support can explain to customers.

sam: one more thought — instrument an internal endpoint that can accept a `debug_key` from a tenant (short-lived) so for debugging we can rehydrate hashed attrs for that session only. make sure it's gated and logged.

maria: careful: rehydration is a compliance landmine. only allow if customer explicitly requests and signs TOS or we have legal approval.

alyssa: noted. will add legal sign-off step in rollout checklist.

kevin: LGTM. small nit: make the collector config conservative for private deployments (no tenant salt default).

alyssa: thanks — will update PR and request reviews. anyone else want to comment before I cut the RFC?

kevin: :thumbsup:

maria: :+1:

sam: looks good

alyssa: tagging for follow-up: @kevin @maria @sam — will drop the PR link here when ready.
